In this appeal, the appellants who are the respondents in O.P.No.537/2018 of the Family Court, Kozhikode call in question the judgment and decree of the said court.
2. Parties shall be referred to by their rank in O.P.537/2018.
3. Petitioner/wife filed O.P.No.537/2018 seeking return of her 15 sovereigns of gold ornaments and Rs.2 lakhs from the husband and father-in-law.
The marriage of the petitioner with the first respondent was solemnized on 19.9.2004 in accordance with the Muslim religious rites and ceremonies.
2 nd respondent is the father of the 1st respondent.
At the time of marriage, petitioner was given 51 sovereigns of gold ornaments and cash of 2 lakhs by her parents.
Respondents were not satisfied with the gold and cash given to the petitioner by her parents and they mentally and physically harassed her demanding more gold and cash.
1 st respondent/husband Mat.A.No.598 of 2021 3 2025:KER:32722 misappropriated 7.5 sovereigns of her gold ornaments and cash of 2 lakhs.

entities.text: A.No.598 of 2021 3 2025:KER:32722 misappropriated 7.5 sovereigns of her gold ornaments and cash of 2 lakhs.
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: 2nd respondent/father-in-law misappropriated another 7.5 sovereigns of her gold ornaments.
Petitioner had lodged a complaint before the police against the respondents and a Crime No.538/2017 under Sections 498A and 406 IPC was registered against the respondents.
Petitioner is entitled to get back her 15 sovereigns of gold and cash of 2 lakhs misappropriated by the respondents.
4. Respondents filed counter-statement denying the allegations regarding misappropriation of the gold ornaments and cash.
They also denied the allegations of cruelty levelled against them.
They also contended that petitioner's family had no financial capacity to give 51 sovereigns of gold ornaments and cash of 2 lakhs.
They contended that whatever gold ornaments petitioner had, it is in her possession and they have not misappropriated it.
5. The Family Court has granted a decree directing the 1 st respondent to return 7.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments and an amount of 2 lakhs to the petitioner.
The 2 nd respondent was directed to return 7.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments to the petitioner.
6. Admittedly, the marriage of the petitioner and 1 st respondent was solemnized on 19.9.2004.

Petitioner who was Mat.A.No.598 of 2021 4 2025:KER:32722 examined as PW1 has testified that at the time of her marriage, she was given 51 sovereigns of gold ornaments and cash of 2 lakhs from her house.

According to her, out of the 51 sovereigns of gold ornaments which she had, 7.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments were misappropriated by her husband/1st respondent in O.P, another 7.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments were misappropriated by her father-in- law/2nd respondent in the O.P.
She has further testified that 1 st respondent also misappropriated the amount of 2 lakhs given to her by her parents at the time of her marriage.

2 7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: PW1 has testified that 1 st respondent misappropriated a pair of gold anklets weighing 32 grams and two bangles weighing 28 grams.
According to her, 1 st respondent sold her gold anklet in 2009 for discharging his loan and he sold her gold bangle, weighing 12 grams in February 2007 for his business purpose.
Her further version is that in July 2013 1 st respondent sold another bangle weighing 16 grams without her knowledge.
Thus, 1 st respondent misappropriated her 7.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments.

She has also testified that 2 nd respondent misappropriated two bangles of 3 sovereigns each and also another bangle weighing 1.5. sovereign for the purpose of raising funds for the construction of the house and also for raising funds to Mat.A.No.598 of 2021 5 2025:KER:32722 send his another son named Tahir abroad.
8. Respondents have no case in their counter statement that petitioner had no gold ornaments at all.
On the other hand, their case is that whatever gold ornaments she had, it was in her possession and they have not taken any gold ornaments.

Though the respondents have raised a contention in their counter statement that the petitioner's family had no financial capacity to give 51 sovereigns of gold and cash to her it is to be borne in mind that while examined as RW1, 1st respondent has admitted that the petitioner's father owned the property facing by-pass road and he had constructed a commercial building in the property.
So, the case canvassed by the respondents that the petitioner's father had no financial capacity to give 51 sovereigns of gold and cash at the time of her marriage is untenable.
9. The specific case of the petitioner is that her gold ornaments, weighing 7.5 sovereigns, were sold by the 1 st respondent to discharge his debt.
1st respondent sold two bangles weighing 28 grams.
RW1 has admitted that he was running a cable TV business during that time.
Further version of PW1 is that her gold anklet, weighing 32 grams, were sold in 2009 for discharging the loan.
RW1 Mat.A.No.598 of 2021 6 2025:KER:32722 has admitted that he had availed loan from South Malabar Gramin Bank and he closed it in the year 2009.
It probabilise the case of the petitioner that by selling her gold anklet weighing 32 grams he discharged the said loan.
Likewise, there is no reason to disbelieve the version of the petitioner that in July 2013, 1 st respondent sold her gold bangle weighing 16 grams without her consent.

PW1 has withstood the test of cross examination and there is no reason to disbelieve the version of the petitioner that her gold ornaments weighing 7.5 sovereigns were misappropriated by the 1st respondent.
10. Many women face situations where gold is misappropriated or forcibly taken by the husband or in-laws.
Due to the informal nature of such transfers, it becomes difficult to prove ownership, if it is not possible for the woman to provide documentary evidence.
In such cases, the Courts rely on the principle of preponderance of probabilities to deliver justice.

11. According to PW1, her father-in-law namely 2 nd respondent took her 7.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments to raise funds for the construction of the house and also to meet the expenses in connection with the sending of his another son abroad.

The version of PW1 that her 15 sovereigns of gold ornaments and 2 lakhs were Mat.A.No.598 of 2021 7 2025:KER:32722 misappropriated by the respondents is credible and trustworthy as held by the learned Family Court and this Court finds no reason to disagree with the said finding.
Hence, we find no reason to interfere with the judgment and decree of the Family Court.
